Cc: procurement@brightlane.ai
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Hosted API pricing inquiry — expected volume spike

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for taking this. Quick background: BrightLane is evaluating a hosted inference partner for our conversational routing product. We expect baseline usage of ~1.2B tokens/month in Q4, with short, predictable spikes up to ~4B tokens/month during promos.

Can you share:
- Baseline per-token pricing for the hosted API (both input/output where you split pricing)
- Whether you offer committed monthly token discounts and sample tiers for that volume
- Overage rules if we go above the commit, and whether burst capacity is included or billed separately
- Typical billing cadence / invoicing for committed plans (monthly/quarterly/annual)

We'd like a ballpark by EOD Tuesday so we can decide whether to take this to procurement. Happy to jump on a short call — my team is available Mon/Tue mornings ET.

Thanks,
Erin Zhao
Head of Platform Partnerships
BrightLane AI
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Zhao <erin@brightlane.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing inquiry — expected volume spike

Hi Erin — great to meet you (virtually). High level answers below; attaching our baseline rate card and a short FAQ that covers commits and billing. (Attachment: redwood_baseline_ratecard_q3.pdf)

Baseline (hosted API, public catalog models):
- List price: $0.0009 / input token, $0.0011 / output token
- For budgeting, many customers use a blended per-token rate; for your expected mix I estimate a blended list rate ~ $0.0010 / token.

Committed discounts (examples for monthly committed tokens):
- 0.25B–1B: 10% off list
- 1B–3B: 18% off list
- 3B–6B: 28% off list
- >6B: custom enterprise pricing and negotiation

Overage & burst behavior:
- Overage: billed at 80% of list price (i.e., a premium above committed unit price but below list), charged monthly.
- Short bursts (up to 2x baseline sustained for <72 hours): automatic burst capacity from shared pool; if bursts are sustained we recommend a temporary capacity uplift or a short-term commit.

Billing cadence / invoicing: monthly billing against committed tokens with end-of-month reconciliation. We also support quarterly and annual prepay for pricing credits.

Next steps I propose:
1) I can send a one-page term sheet with a two-tier commit schedule tailored to your Q4 profile.
2) If you're open, let's schedule a 30-minute call Monday 9:30am ET to walk through usage patterns and SLA requirements.

Sharing this to Ben for an Ops perspective.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Thanks Lauren — super helpful. A couple of quick clarifications before we schedule:
- In your examples the 1B–3B tier (18% off) — is that based on committed tokens being consumed or committed capacity (i.e., we pay for the commit even if unused)?
- Can you give a quick example invoice calculation for a month where we commit 1.5B but consume 2.8B?
- Any SLA credits tied to latency or availability breaches at sustained throughput? We are sensitive to sub-200ms tail latency for routing decisions.

Also attached is a sample monthly usage CSV that shows our baseline vs. promo spikes to help you tailor the tiering if needed. (Attachment: brightlane_usage_sample.csv)

Appreciate the Monday 9:30am slot — that works for us.

—Erin
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, marcuS_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 13:02:00 -0400
Subject: Internal: BrightLane pricing suggested structure

Lauren / Marcus — quick internal thought before Monday:
- Recommend we propose a phased commit: Q4 ramp commit 1.2B/mo for first two months at 18% off; then automatic step-up to 3B/mo at 25% off if average of prior 30 days >2.5B. This reduces BrightLane's cash burden while giving us predictable capacity.
- For month-over-month overage, bill at list*0.8 but cap effective overage rate to blended committed rate + 30% to avoid bill shock.
- SLA: offer a 99.9% uptime SLO + latency credit tiers (0.5% credit if 95–99.9% tail latency <=200ms; 1.5% credit if >200ms more than X) — need to confirm exact wording with SRE.

I'll be on the call Monday and can cover sustained throughput implications (queueing, caching recommendations).

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Hi Erin — per our call this morning (thanks everyone) here is a concise proposal and next steps. Attached above is the same baseline rate card; below is the proposed commit schedule tailored to BrightLane's Q4 profile.

Proposed commercial terms (summary):
- Initial pilot commit (months 1–2): 1.2B tokens/month at 18% off list
- Scale trigger: if 30-day rolling consumption >2.5B, auto-increase to a 3B/month commit at 25% off list
- Sustained high-tier: 3B–6B commit at 28% off list; >6B requires custom negotiation
- Overage mechanics: per-token overage billed at 0.8 * list price, but not exceeding (committed effective rate + 30%) to avoid sudden spikes in invoice.
- Billing: monthly invoices with reconciliation; option for quarter prepay with 2% additional discount on committed spend.
- SLA: Redwood will include a 99.9% uptime SLO for inference endpoints in the proposal. For tail latency commitments, we propose credits as Ben suggested — we will circulate SRE-approved wording in the formal term sheet.

Next steps:
1) I will upload a one-page commercial term sheet to the proposal link and share by EOD today (link: https://docs.redwood.inference.com/proposals/BL-2026-0828).
2) If that looks good, procurement can send standard PO language; our legal team will then attach standard T&Cs.
3) Ben to follow up with a short ops note outlining caching and batching recommendations that will materially reduce cost for your burst profile.

If you want, we can include a 60-day pilot credit to cover initial testing traffic; I can surface that on the term sheet.

Would you prefer we prepare an estimate invoice for a representative month (commit 1.5B, consume 2.8B) — I can include that as well.

Best regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
